title: When the Weather Breaks
premise: Dominic Iversen has spent thirty years tuning pianos in other people's houses, listening through the walls to lives louder than their own, while keeping their own history locked behind a smile that ends conversations. When a stranger at their mother's funeral addresses the family by a name nobody has used since 1987—the name they buried along with a crime no one was ever charged for—Dominic realizes someone else survived that night and has been waiting decades to be acknowledged. As the stranger's letters grow more insistent and a cold-case journalist circles closer, Dominic must finally speak the truth of what their family did to stay invisible: they let an innocent man take the blame. The novel ends with Dominic testifying, imperfectly and too late, at a parole hearing—choosing a name, a story, and a self over the safety of silence.
about_author: Ines Halloran is a former piano technician who spent fifteen years working in the houses of strangers before turning to fiction full-time. She writes about quiet people and the debts they carry, and lives near the coast with a restored upright piano she refuses to tune for anyone else.

chapters.title: The Tuner's Ear
chapters.summary: Dominic Iversen tunes a dead client's piano in an empty house, reading the family's history in radiators, water stains, and worn keys. POV: Dominic. Establishes their gift for hearing what others hide and their practiced smile. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; the reader senses a life built on avoidance.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: At their mother's funeral, a gaunt stranger named Ada Kowalczyk approaches the receiving line and says, 'You're the Fenwicks, aren't you?' Dominic's brother Marcus goes white; the old name hasn't been spoken aloud in decades. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out—the past arriving in daylight, uninvited.

chapters.title: What the Family Agreed To
chapters.summary: After the funeral, siblings Marcus, Nell, and Dominic meet in the childhood kitchen and rehearse the official version of 1987: a fire, an accident, a man named Teodor Lindqvist who 'did his time.' Their stories don't quite match. POV: rotating among the three siblings. Emotional beat: complicity surfacing as irritation; each sibling remembers a different crime.

chapters.title: Letters from Ada
chapters.summary: Ada's first letter arrives: she is Teodor's daughter, and she doesn't want money—she wants to know what really happened the night her father took the blame for a death in the Fenwick house. Dominic burns it, then retrieves it from the sink. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: guilt with nowhere to put itself; the first crack in the perfected silence.

chapters.title: The Houses We Tune
chapters.summary: Back at work, Dominic can't stop hearing confessions in clients' homes—a hidden second staircase, a child's height marks painted over. A flashback thread begins: young Dominic, age nine, hiding under the stairs the night everything changed. POV: Dominic, present and past. Emotional beat: memory as sound; the past is literally audible.

chapters.title: Nell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Nell, the eldest, who orchestrated the cover-up as a nineteen-year-old, visits Dominic with an envelope of cash for Ada and a warning: some doors stay shut because opening them kills everyone in the room. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: love expressed as control; the reader sees how survival calcified into tyranny.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: A local reporter, Priya Raman, researching a piece on wrongful convictions, contacts Marcus about the Lindqvist case—Teodor served eleven years for arson and manslaughter and died without exoneration. Marcus stonewalls, badly. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: panic wearing the mask of respectability; the outside world closing in.

chapters.title: Under the Stairs, 1987
chapters.summary: A full flashback chapter: nine-year-old Dominic watches from the dark as their father starts the fire that kills a lodger—and as the adults agree, in whispers, that Teodor, the lodger's friend with a record, will be blamed. POV: young Dominic. Emotional beat: the moment innocence ended; the origin of the smile that ends conversations.

chapters.title: Meeting Ada
chapters.summary: Against Nell's orders, Dominic meets Ada at a diner. She isn't vengeful—she's exhausted, carrying her father's unanswered questions like furniture she can't put down. She asks only one thing: tell me the truth so he can rest. POV: alternating Dominic and Ada. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness between the keeper of a secret and its orphan.

chapters.title: The Smile Fails
chapters.summary: Dominic tries to work and cannot; mid-tuning, they break down in a stranger's living room and confess nothing but weep anyway. The client, an old woman, says simply, 'Whatever it is, it gets heavier the longer you hold it.' POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: collapse of the armor; grief finally given permission.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Marcus, terrified of exposure, secretly offers Priya a partial story that pins everything on their dead father—protecting himself by sacrificing the family myth. Dominic learns of it and realizes the secret is now a weapon pointed inward. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: betrayal as self-preservation; the family eating itself.

chapters.title: What Teodor Carried
chapters.summary: Ada shares her father's prison letters: he knew he was taking the blame—he agreed to it, paid off, believing the Fenwicks' child had set the fire and deserved protecting. He thought he was shielding Dominic. POV: Ada, through documents and memory. Emotional beat: devastating reversal—the sacrifice was a gift, misread for thirty years.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts Nell with the truth of the payoff. Nell finally admits she chose Teodor not to protect Dominic but to protect the family's name, and has spent her life paying for that arithmetic. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: the villain revealed as the first casualty; pity where there was only anger.

chapters.title: Priya's Draft
chapters.summary: Priya sends Marcus a draft of her article: 'The Fire at Fenwick House.' Publication is two weeks out. The siblings face the choice—be exposed on someone else's terms or come forward on their own. POV: rotating siblings. Emotional beat: the clock starting; silence now costs more than speech.

chapters.title: Tuning Fork
chapters.summary: Dominic returns to the sold Fenwick house, now stripped to studs, and stands in the room where it happened. They realize they've spent their life tuning other people's instruments because their own voice was confiscated at nine years old. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the decision forming—not courage yet, but the shape of it.

chapters.title: The Family Vote
chapters.summary: In the kitchen one last time, the siblings vote: Nell says silence, Marcus says spin, and Dominic—for the first time in the novel—says the true thing out loud: 'I saw him light it. I'm going to say so.' POV: all three. Emotional beat: the fracture becoming a choice; the middle sibling finally leading.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: Dominic gives Priya a sworn statement naming their father and exonerating Teodor, knowing it may bring charges against the estate and shame on them all. Marcus withdraws his counter-story; Nell refuses to sign but doesn't stop them. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into agency; the smile retired for good.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: The article publishes. Old clients cancel; a nephew stops calling; but strangers write—children of other silent families, thanking them. An investigator reopens the case file. POV: Dominic and brief chorus of voices. Emotional beat: loss and liberation arriving together; identity rebuilt in public.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: At Teodor's posthumous exoneration review, Dominic testifies—haltingly, incompletely, honestly—while Ada sits in the front row. Nell appears at the back door but does not enter. The board clears Teodor's name. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the climax; justice delivered late, imperfect, and still real.

chapters.title: What Nell Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Nell leaves Dominic a letter—no apology, but the full account of 1987 in her own hand, ending with 'I would do it worse now.' Dominic reads it twice and keeps it. POV: Nell via letter, Dominic frame. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution; the family's ledger finally balanced, if never settled.

chapters.title: A Proper Goodbye
chapters.summary: Dominic and Ada visit Teodor's grave together, bringing a small tuned chime that plays when the wind crosses it. They say goodbye properly, at last, out loud—his name, her father, their debt. POV: shared. Emotional beat: mourning completed; the secret transformed into a shared inheritance.

chapters.title: Dominic Iversen, Tuner
chapters.summary: Months later, Dominic tunes a piano in a bright house and, asked who they are, answers plainly—with their name, their work, and none of the old smile. The last note hangs in the warm air, true pitch at last. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: resolution; a self chosen rather than survived, and the quiet after a long dissonance resolves.
